questions.prompt: Identify the design tool that would include a process box.
questions.markSchemeHint: A) Flow chart (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Identify one hardware consideration when designing a Human Computer Interface (HCI).
questions.markSchemeHint: Display/screen size, resolution, memory (RAM), processor/CPU, battery life, input/output devices.

questions.prompt: Identify one digital platform that could be used to store stock records.
questions.markSchemeHint: Database (or spreadsheet).

questions.scenarioContext: Choose two terms from: double entry, format check, manual checking, range check.
questions.prompt:
Complete the following sentence:
Data verification is carried out using [Blank 1] and [Blank 2] tools.
questions.markSchemeHint: double entry (1) and manual checking (1).

questions.scenarioContext: A portable USB flash drive is one type of external storage device.
questions.prompt: Identify two other external storage devices.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: external hard disk drive (HDD), external solid-state drive (SSD), SD/memory card, optical disc (CD/DVD/Blu-ray), magnetic tape.

questions.prompt: Identify the validation tool that checks for the correct number of characters during data entry.
questions.markSchemeHint: Length check.

questions.prompt: What does 2FA stand for?
questions.markSchemeHint: Two-Factor Authentication.

questions.prompt: Identify the type of malware that displays unwanted advertisements on a mobile device.
questions.markSchemeHint: Adware.

questions.prompt: Identify the legislation that covers the physical use of computer hardware for work purposes.
questions.markSchemeHint: Health and Safety at Work Act (1974) / Display Screen Equipment (DSE) Regulations.

questions.prompt: What is Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) used for?
questions.markSchemeHint: Making voice (and video) calls / transmitting speech over the internet.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of an audience demographic?
questions.markSchemeHint: A) Accessibility (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Link the Internet of Everything (IoE) interactivity to the correct example. (You will only use two examples.)
matchingRight: Laptop wirelessly sending instructions to a printer
questions.markSchemeHint: D2D -> Laptop wirelessly sending instructions to a printer (1); H2D -> Interaction with a digital assistant (1).

questions.scenarioContext: A wearable fitness device allows a user to track their activity levels. One type of fitness device can be worn on the wrist of the user. The device can provide: date and time, number of steps taken each day, number of active minutes each day.
questions.prompt: Explain the purpose of having a HCI within the wearable fitness device.
questions.markSchemeHint: Allows the user to interact with/control the device (1) and view/read their real-time fitness outputs such as steps, time, and active minutes clearly on their wrist (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Wearable fitness device worn on the wrist.
questions.prompt: Explain two disadvantages of having a HCI within the wearable fitness device.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each: very small screen makes text/metrics hard to read or buttons easy to mis-tap; screen drains battery life faster; increases manufacturing/purchase cost; fragile screen can scratch/crack during exercise.

questions.prompt: Other than touch, identify one method of user interaction that could be used for the HCI on the wearable fitness device.
questions.markSchemeHint: Voice, gesture (wrist raise/shake), or physical buttons/crown.

questions.scenarioContext: The wearable fitness device links to an account accessed through a new website where users see all their fitness data.
questions.prompt: Explain two disadvantages to a user of using the website to view their personal fitness information.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each: requires internet connection and browser/device to log in; cyber-security/privacy risk if account is hacked; less convenient than glancing at wrist/app while exercising; website downtime prevents access.

questions.scenarioContext: The user will input information when they log on to the website.
questions.prompt: Describe the difference between data and information.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data is raw, unprocessed facts/figures with no meaning on its own (1), whereas information is data that has been processed with context and structure so it has meaning (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Choose two words from: accuracy, modification, presenting, processing.
questions.prompt:
Complete the following sentence:
Data validation checks [Blank 1] before [Blank 2] the data.
questions.markSchemeHint: accuracy (1) before processing (1).

questions.scenarioContext:
After a user has logged into the new website they can change how the website's homepage will look each time they log in. Information shown includes:
• their name and photograph
• the number of steps taken that day
• the number of active minutes that day
• the amount of sleep they had that day
questions.prompt:
Create a wireframe to plan the layout and content for the user's homepage.
Marks will be awarded for: content; layout.
questions.markSchemeHint: Up to 4 marks Content (header/nav, name & photo placeholder, widgets/cards for daily steps, active minutes, sleep, customisation/edit layout button, logout/settings, annotations) and up to 4 marks Layout (clear desktop/web frame, clean wireframe boxes/placeholders, balanced grid, logical visual hierarchy).

questions.scenarioContext:
Before a new website is published user testing will be carried out. The registration page will be tested so users can only enter:
• a valid email address
• a valid password with 8–12 characters and a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers
• a valid username with a minimum of 5 characters.
questions.prompt: Complete the table with examples of what test data could be used. Justify the test data you have chosen.
questions.markSchemeHint: 3 marks per row (1 concrete test value + 2 marks justification explaining what rule/boundary it tests): e.g., Test 1 'alex@mail.co.uk' (valid format with @ and domain); Test 2 'FitPass12' (9 chars—within 8–12 with upper, lower, numbers); Test 3 'Alex1' (5 chars—boundary test for minimum 5 characters).

questions.scenarioContext: Users can access the fitness website on different devices.
questions.prompt: Identify two characteristics of smartphones that make them suitable for accessing the website.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: portable/lightweight, built-in Wi-Fi and mobile data (4G/5G), web browser support, touchscreen interface, long battery life.

questions.scenarioContext: Accessing personal fitness information on the website.
questions.prompt: Explain how a username and password will help keep the user's personal fitness information secure.
questions.markSchemeHint: Authenticates the user's identity (1) so only authorised account holders with the correct secret credentials can access their personal fitness data (1).

questions.prompt: Other than usernames and passwords, identify two other logical prevention measures.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: encryption (HTTPS/SSL), two-factor authentication (2FA), firewall, anti-malware, access levels, automatic session timeout, secure backups.

questions.scenarioContext: The manufacturer of a wearable fitness device is designing an upgrade and will use an online survey stored in the Cloud to collect ideas from registered users.
questions.prompt: Explain one advantage to the registered users of an online survey being used to collect this data.
questions.markSchemeHint: 1 mark point + 1 mark expansion: convenient—users can complete it anytime/anywhere on their own device; quick to submit without postage/travel; gives users a direct voice in shaping future features.

questions.scenarioContext: The survey will include images sourced from other websites to show ideas for future upgrades.
questions.prompt: Describe two actions that will need to be taken to comply with the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each: ask/obtain written permission from the copyright owner before using the image; pay any required licence/royalty fee; credit/acknowledge the original creator/source; use royalty-free or Creative Commons licensed images.

questions.scenarioContext: Survey data stored in the Cloud.
questions.prompt: Identify two disadvantages to the manufacturer of storing the data in a cloud storage location.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: ongoing subscription/storage costs, requires reliable internet access, reliance on third-party security/uptime, data protection/jurisdiction concerns.

questions.scenarioContext: Users can now share access to their wearable fitness device and website account with a personal fitness trainer using the Internet of Everything (IoE). Shared data includes: when users exercise, where users exercise, heart rate, number of active minutes each day.
questions.prompt:
Discuss the suitability of using the IoE to share health and fitness data with a personal fitness trainer.

In your answer you must consider:
• the purpose of the IoE
• the advantages of using the IoE to share health and fitness data
• the disadvantages of using the IoE to share health and fitness data.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 9-mark Level of Response (L1: 1–3, L2: 4–6, L3: 7–9). Purpose: seamlessly connects people, process, data, and wearable things to automatically collect and share live data. Advantages: real-time heart rate/activity tracking lets trainer tailor workouts accurately, remote coaching/motivation, automatic syncing without manual logging. Disadvantages: serious privacy/safety risks (sharing exact exercise times & GPS locations!), sensitive health data vulnerable to cyber-attacks/breaches, depends on internet/battery/accurate sensors. Reasoned conclusion.
